text: Barabási & Albert's 1999 Science paper 'Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks' is significant because it...
choices: Introduced the Watts-Strogatz model interpolating between regular lattices and random graphs
Defined modularity Q as a metric for evaluating community detection
Introduced the Louvain algorithm for large-scale community detection
Proposed preferential attachment as a mechanism generating scale-free networks, helping explain why hub proteins are common and evolutionarily persistent
explanation: Barabási & Albert proposed the preferential-attachment growth mechanism ('rich get richer') that generates scale-free, power-law degree distributions, motivating why a small number of highly connected hub proteins tend to arise and persist in evolving biological networks. The Watts-Strogatz small-world model is a separate contribution not from this paper, and modularity Q and the Louvain algorithm are community-detection concepts introduced by different, later work.
